To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the implementation of routine HIV screening in an urban emergency department resulted in a 3% increase in HIV testing, with 1.2% of individuals testing HIV positive.
(1) HIV screening in the emergency department is associated with a high yield of positive test results and (2) the implementation of opt-out HIV testing in the emergency department can be successful.

(1) the proportion of patients tested for HIV in the ED increased after the CDC released its 2006 guidelines, (2) the proportion of ED patients tested for HIV was significantly associated with patient age, race, insurance status, and HIV risk factors, (3) ED testing rates were highest in urban EDs and lowest in rural EDs, and (4) ED testing rates varied by state and region.
